correctness.rationale: The 31 2-facets match Lutz 1999 dissertation p.18 (PDF physical p.23) exactly, including the ten-vertex labels. An independently implemented oriented-boundary construction, distinct from the bundled verifier, gives full f=(10,40,31), ranks (rank d1,rank d2)=(9,31), and Betti_Q=(1,0,0). For all ten vertex deletions, exact rational matrix ranks yield beta0=1, beta2=0 and beta1=(3,3,3,3,3,2,2,2,1,1) on v=1,...,10. The deletion face vectors are (9,31,20) on 1,5; (9,32,21) on 2,3,4; (9,32,22) on 6,7,8; (9,33,24) on 9,10. Thus the claim is fully finite and exhaustive. Independently, every graph link is connected with cycle rank t_v-e_v+1; Mayer-Vietoris for X=(X-v) union cone(link v), plus acyclicity of X, identifies H1(X-v;Q) with H1(link v;Q). Actual link edge/vertex data are (11,9) on 1,5; (10,8) on 2,3,4; (9,8) on 6,7,8; and (7,7) on 9,10. This second derivation agrees. The primary source, not the finite verifier, supplies noncontractibility of the undeleted X. No integral-torsion or deletion homotopy classification is claimed.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge statement comparison found the printed original 31-facet complex and its global Z-acyclic noncontractible property in Lutz (1999), and the same 10,40,31 global example in later topology literature, but no inspected statement establishes the entire ten-vertex rational deletion-H1 profile. Published Resultary findings concerning deletion landscapes/punctures have other objects, coefficients, or deletion operations, not a stronger theorem about these ten induced deletions. The ranks are elementary computations from available facets, but the rank table itself is not copied from an identified prior source; mathematical determinacy from raw source data is distinguished from an already-stated result. Journal full text was not inspected in entirety, and possible historical unindexed equivalent computations remain residual risks.

value.rationale: The ten-vertex acyclic noncontractible model was introduced as a compressed triangulation of an identified-dodecahedron Poincaré-type 2-complex, with explicit concern for vertex economy. Whether any vertex can be removed while retaining rational acyclicity is therefore a natural local irredundancy test, not an arbitrary slice. The complete answer is sharp for every one of the ten vertices: none has an acyclic induced deletion, and their nontrivial H1 defects split into three precisely identified levels 3^5,2^3,1^2. A subsequent researcher comparing local reductions, link complexity or vertex-deletion strategies could need this exact labeled profile. The computation itself is modest and does not address global minimality or homotopy equivalence under moves; significance is restricted to this canonical finite example and its single-vertex local structure. It is neither a generic theorem nor a claim that routine homological identities are new.

limitations: No general vertex-minimality among all noncontractible Z-acyclic complexes was proved or claimed.
Deletion rational homology is established, not deletion integral torsion or homotopy type; full X noncontractibility taken from Lutz source.
